newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly gain again on hot weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly gain again on hot weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to up slightly again Monday in moderate activity, with continued heat on the East Coast and forecasts for more through the week still lifting the complex.
"Low sulphur seems to be jumping. There's some life in low sulphur because of the heat," said one cash trader, noting some East Coast utilities quietly were looking for more barrels.
In New York Harbor, reports a local utility was looking for 75-80,000 barrels of 0.3 high pour helped boost prices another 25-50 cents to about $18.25 a barrel, traders said.

A Mid-Atlantic utility bought 30,000 barrels of prompt 0.5 percent material at an index-related price less a small discount and reportedly was looking for another 50,000 barrels. In addition, a New England utility late last week was reported looking for 225,000 barrels of 0.7 percent for second-half July delivery.

Physical one percent in New York held steady at $16.25-50, with July one percent paper gaining another 30 cents to $16.70-90 on firmer crude. August paper also was quoted higher at $16.45-65, with Sept at $16.25-50 and Q4 at $16.65-85.
High sulphurs in New York firmed slightly, with 2.2 percent now quoted on either side of $14.75.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with three percent still at $13.25-50 and one percent at $15.25-50.

New York city gate gas prices held relatively steady Monday in the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.50 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was talked in the $2.17/mmBtu area, or $13.67 a barrel.
